forces.title: Strong structural demand for nursing home beds due to demographics.
forces.description: Ireland's aging population and increased life expectancy are driving exceptionally strong demand for residential care, with average occupancy in nursing homes reaching 94.9%. This fundamental demographic trend creates a robust, long-term tailwind for healthcare real estate property owners, underpinning consistent demand for nursing home beds and supporting sustained investment activity in the sector. The structural nature of this demand ensures continued relevance and growth potential for asset owners.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Rising costs and regulatory pressure squeeze nursing home profitability.
forces.description: Nursing home property owners in Ireland face significant pressure on profitability due to rising staff costs, which represent 60.9% of revenue, coupled with general operating cost inflation and increased regulatory burdens. Although Fair Deal rates have seen increases, they frequently lag behind the escalating expenses, resulting in a squeeze on margins. This economic headwind challenges the financial viability and operational efficiency of asset owners in the healthcare real estate sector.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Persistent capacity constraints drive investment in nursing home properties.
forces.description: Ireland faces a persistent and significant capacity gap in its residential care sector, with the national nursing home bed stock having declined and an estimated 1,039 additional beds required annually. This undersupply, combined with robust demographic-driven demand, acts as a strong tailwind, attracting substantial investment activity and supporting premium valuations for modern healthcare real estate facilities, providing opportunities for property owners to expand and develop assets.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Phased return of state-contracted hotels boosts tourism supply.
forces.description: The gradual withdrawal of state-contracted commercial accommodation, previously used for temporary protection and international protection, is steadily returning registered tourism bed stock to the market by March 2027. This phased release of capacity provides a positive supply-side tailwind for Irish hotel real estate property owners, improving overall destination capacity. While the impact will vary geographically, it offers a measured increase in commercial supply, supporting revenue potential.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Market polarization defines investment in Irish hotel real estate.
forces.description: Ireland's hotel real estate market is undergoing a structural shift characterized by pronounced market polarization. Strongest investor and customer momentum is concentrated at the luxury/lifestyle and budget/value segments. This trend pressures mid-market and independent hotel property owners to strategically reposition, seek brand affiliations, or offer distinctive experience-led differentiation to protect their relevance and pricing power. Failing to adapt to this polarization could lead to reduced demand and investment for non-specialized assets.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Capital investment shifts to hotel enhancement over new-build expansion.
forces.description: Capital investment in Ireland's hotel real estate sector is structurally shifting from speculative new-build expansion towards enhancement of existing assets. Property owners are prioritizing refurbishment, repositioning, energy efficiency upgrades, and improvements to guest experience. This strategy aims to optimize existing portfolios, increase asset value, and align with sustainability goals, rather than incurring the higher costs and risks associated with new construction in the current investment environment.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Strategic M&A opportunities for well-capitalized hotel real estate groups.
forces.description: The Irish hotel real estate market presents opportunistic M&A activity, particularly favorable for well-capitalized groups. These entities are better positioned to acquire or reinvest in assets where smaller operators face pressure from cost inflation, succession issues, or significant capital expenditure requirements. This environment creates an upside driver for strategic players to expand their portfolios through consolidation, enhance operational efficiencies, and unlock value in properties needing repositioning or upgrades.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Geopolitical disruption poses direct risk to hotel real estate demand.
forces.description: Geopolitical risk, exacerbated by global conflicts like the Middle East crisis, represents a direct and significant key risk for Irish hotel real estate demand. A sustained deterioration in geopolitical conditions could weigh heavily on inbound tourism sentiment, reduce corporate travel confidence, increase airfares, and diminish high-value long-haul demand. This directly translates to potential revenue volatility and reduced RevPAR for hotel property owners, impacting their operational and financial stability.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Higher energy and transport costs pressure healthcare real estate margins.
forces.description: Healthcare real estate, encompassing energy-intensive residential and hospital care settings in Ireland, faces significant margin pressure from sustained energy price volatility and rising transport costs, largely due to indirect impacts of the Middle East crisis on global supply chains. As the sector has limited ability to pass through these escalating operating expenses, primarily due to public funding mechanisms, it directly challenges the profitability and financial viability of healthcare property owners.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Consolidation and public funding drive investment in nursing home real estate.
forces.description: Investment activity across Ireland's health sector is robust, characterized by ongoing consolidation within nursing homes, with group ownership now accounting for approximately 58% of private beds. Furthermore, substantial public capital investment, including €9.25 billion committed to health infrastructure under the National Development Plan (2026–2030), provides a strong tailwind. This supports property owners focused on scaling, asset quality, and managing increasingly complex operational requirements within healthcare real estate.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Investment shifts to existing facility upgrades due to cost inflation.
forces.description: Across the Irish healthcare real estate sector, capital investment is exhibiting a cyclical shift, increasingly concentrating on improving existing facilities through refurbishment, energy efficiency upgrades, and administrative digitalization. This trend represents a move away from new-build expansion, primarily driven by persistent construction cost inflation, stringent planning and regulatory constraints, and an overall cautious investment environment. This influences development strategies and asset utilization for property owners.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Ireland's healthcare real estate outlook positive, driven by strong demographic demand.
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland maintains a positive outlook for Ireland's healthcare sector, particularly for property owners in residential care and disability services. Favorable demographics, including an aging population and increasing chronic disease incidence, ensure robust demand. Significant capacity gaps in nursing homes (1,039 beds annually needed) and residential disability places (2,197 additional places required) underpin strong investor confidence, consolidation, and high valuations for modern facilities, supporting continued investment in specialized healthcare real estate assets.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Ireland's hotel real estate sees cautious positive outlook with market polarization.
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland notes a cautiously positive outlook for Ireland's hotel real estate, driven by rate-led RevPAR growth and gradually increasing tourism supply as state-contracted accommodation returns to the market. While overall performance is positive, market polarization is pronounced, favoring luxury/lifestyle and budget/value segments. Investors and operators prioritize assets with clear paths to operational improvement, repositioning, and energy efficiency. Challenges include shorter booking windows and the need for mid-market hotels to differentiate, indicating selective investment opportunities for property owners.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.driver: Aging population and increased life expectancy
demand_drivers.description: Ireland’s ageing population, increased life expectancy, and rising incidence of chronic disease continue to underpin growth in residential care demand.

new_opportunities.description: An estimated 1,039 nursing home beds are required annually to meet future demand in Ireland.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Meeting future nursing home bed demand

market_sizing.methodology: ESRI projects annual requirement of 1,039 additional nursing home beds, calculated based on Ireland's aging population, increased life expectancy, and rising chronic disease incidence driving future demand for residential care.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: Disability services in Ireland are experiencing sustained growth, with an estimated 38,288 adults accessing HSE-funded services, increasing annually by 10%.

new_opportunities.description: Need for 2,197 additional residential disability places, representing a significant healthcare infrastructure opportunity for property owners.

market_sizing.methodology: Current planning estimates indicate a requirement for an additional 2,197 residential disability places based on sustained growth in demand for disability services.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: Continued positive RevPAR trends in ROI locations, high average occupancy in Dublin, and higher average room rates in regions support accommodation sales performance.

pnl_drivers.description: Average room rates (ADR) are the main growth driver for hotel real estate revenues in regional Irish markets, while occupancy levels primarily drive performance in Dublin.

market_sizing.methodology: Accommodation sales performance based on CoStar STR June 2026 data, detailing RevPAR trends, average room rates, and occupancy levels across various Irish markets for Q1 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026
